statutorySection: Ind AS 102 (Share-based Payment) converged with IFRS 2 and aligned with US GAAP ASC 718
title: Share-Based Payments & Employee Stock Options (ESOP Grant-Date Fair Value & Graded Vesting Amortization)

effectivePeriod.annualReset: Annual vesting tranche evaluation, forfeiture true-ups, and equity reserve roll-forward at reporting dates
effectivePeriod.sunsetNotes: Mandatory standard notified via MCA G.S.R. 111(E) effective FY 2015-16 onwards.

plainTextSummary: Under Ind AS 102 (converged with IFRS 2 and aligned with US GAAP ASC 718), equity-settled share-based payment transactions (such as Employee Stock Option Plans / ESOPs) must be measured at the grant-date fair value of the equity instruments granted, typically determined using an option pricing model such as Black-Scholes-Merton (BSM) or a binomial lattice model. For equity-settled awards, the fair value is fixed at grant date and is not subsequently remeasured for changes in stock price. Where awards vest in tranches over multiple years (graded vesting, e.g. 25% each year over 4 years), Ind AS 102 mandates that each tranche must be treated as a separate award with its own distinct service period, resulting in front-loaded compensation expense in profit or loss rather than a single straight-line average over the total 4 years. For cross-border structures (e.g. US Delaware Parent issuing options to employees of its Indian operating subsidiary), the transaction is accounted for in the subsidiary as an equity contribution from the parent credit to Share-Based Payment Reserve and a debit to Employee Benefit Expense, subject to intercompany recharge agreements. Under Indian Income Tax law, the employee is subject to salary TDS under Section 192 read with Section 17(2)(vi) and Rule 3(8) on the exercise date based on Fair Market Value (FMV) determined by a SEBI-registered Category-I Merchant Banker minus exercise price; meanwhile, the company is entitled to claim ESOP discount as an allowable business deduction under Section 37(1) across the vesting period pursuant to the Supreme Court affirmation of the Special Bench ruling in CIT v. Biocon Ltd.
